songs.name: It's All Over Now Baby Blue

ai_show_review.summary: Marathon Lovelight caps a raw, jam‑heavy '69 set
ai_show_review.blurb: The night opens with a soaring Dark Star and tight Saint Stephen before diving into an expansive The Eleven. A rough China Cat Sunflower/High Time transition leads to a marathon 35‑minute Turn On Your Lovelight that dominates the second set. Despite tape hiss and occasional distortion, the performance captures raw early‑Dead power.
ai_show_review.review: July 5, 1969 at Chicago’s Electric Theater showcases the Grateful Dead in an unapologetically raw phase of their evolution. The first set rockets off with a soaring Dark Star that lets Jerry stretch his improvisational muscles, followed by a tight Saint Stephen and an adventurous take on The Eleven before slipping into a brief but heartfelt rendition of It’s All Over Now Baby Blue. The second set is a mixed bag – the China Cat Sunflower/High Time segue feels a little rough around the edges, yet the band pulls together for a blistering run through Mama Tried, Hard To Handle and Casey Jones that sets up the show‑ending monster: an unbroken 35‑minute Turn On Your Lovelight that swells and recedes with the kind of collective intensity only this era could produce. The recording is a mud‑covered soundboard capture; hiss, tape wobble and occasional vocal distortion (notably on Momma Tried) are audible, but the stereo mix still offers enough clarity to hear the interplay, especially during the extended Lovelight. For listeners willing to tolerate some sonic grime, this document provides a vivid snapshot of the Dead’s early jam‑heavy ethos.

best_recording.reason: Only soundboard source; despite tape hiss and wobble it captures the full set including the epic 35‑minute Lovelight.

key_highlights: Epic Dark Star jam that showcases raw Garcia energy.
Marathon 35‑minute Turn On Your Lovelight closing the show.
Strong early set with Saint Stephen, The Eleven and a tight China Cat Sunflower/High Time transition.

band_performance.Jerry: Shows raw power in Dark Star but sounds out of sorts on Saint Stephen and The Eleven, flubbing or eliding key phrases.
